subject: PromptPilot x Redwood: LangChain adapter + runtime tracing pilot
messages:
From: Emma Lee <emma@promptpilot.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: PromptPilot x Redwood: LangChain adapter + runtime tracing pilot

Hi Mina,

I lead Partnerships at PromptPilot — we build a developer-facing prompt orchestration and retrieval layer that teams embed in chat-oriented products. We recently rebuilt our runtime to rely on a LangChain SDK-based connector model (LangChain + LlamaIndex compatibility) and are looking to validate tight integration with Redwood's serving runtime for lower latency and better observability.

High-level ask: run a technical pilot to build a lightweight LangChain adapter + runtime tracing hooks so our customers can use PromptPilot with Redwood as a recommended deployment. Goals:
- End-to-end demo (LangChain app -> PromptPilot -> Redwood hosted inference)
- Trace visibility for request flow and token costs
- Performance baseline for chat+retrieval workloads (streaming enabled)

We sketched an integration brief (attached) and can share sample traffic patterns. Would Redwood be open to a 4-6 week pilot and a joint mutual action plan?

Suggested next step: 30-45m technical sync next week (we're PST). I'm copying our partnerships alias for scheduling.

Attachments: promptpilot-integration-brief.pdf

Thanks,
Emma Lee
VP, Partnerships
PromptPilot
emma@promptpilot.ai
https://promptpilot.ai

Hey Emma — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for the brief. Vanessa (partnerships) and Jonas (runtime engineer) are looped in.

We'd be interested in a pilot. Quick notes from our side:
- Redwood can provide a staging tenant and short-lived API keys for a PoC.
- We have an SDK adapter pattern we've used for LangChain/LlamaIndex partners; typical connector is ~2-3 dev days for a minimal adapter but tracing hooks & streaming considerations add effort.
- We prefer a MAP that includes success metrics (p95 latency improvement target, error budget, and visibility checklist).

Could you share your preferred NDA/SOW template and any traffic matrices? Vanessa, can you check available windows for a 45m sync next Tue/Wed PST? Jonas — once we have traffic numbers, can you advise on cost/throughput expectations?

I've attached a connector checklist to help scope.

Attachments: redwood-connector-checklist.docx

Best,
Mina Haddad

Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PromptPilot x Redwood: LangChain adapter + runtime tracing pilot

Emma / Mina — thanks for looping me in. A few technical clarifying questions so we can size the effort and identify risk: 
1) Which LangChain runtime version and which LangChain connectors are you using? Are you pinning to a specific LlamaIndex version?
2) Do you expect streaming token-by-token responses (server-sent events / chunked)? Any client-side constraints (mobile web vs server)?
3) Traffic profile: steady RPS vs burstable; average and 95th percentile request size (tokens) would help.
4) Are you using custom sampling/rewrites in PromptPilot that change tokenization (we've seen delta in token counts based on prompt templates)?
5) For tracing: do you need payload-level logging (redacted text) or only request/response IDs and timing metrics?

From Redwood's perspective we can:
- Provide a sample adapter repo with test harness.
- Add lightweight tracing hooks (trace id propagation + token accounting events) that surface in Console.

If you can share answers and a traffic CSV, I can draft a one-page SOW checklist for the sync.

—Jonas
Lead Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Lee <emma@promptpilot.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: partners@promptpilot.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PromptPilot x Redwood: LangChain adapter + runtime tracing pilot

Hi Mina / Jonas — thanks for the quick replies. Answers inline below and attached a traffic matrix CSV.

Jonas — answers:
1) LangChain: 0.0.105 (we've forked a small shim for connector lifecycle). LlamaIndex: 0.8.x for retrieval.
2) Streaming: yes — majority of sessions use streaming websocket or SSE to the client. We can fall back to non-streaming for PoC but would prefer streaming in later stages.
3) Traffic: nominal 8–12 RPS per customer, but expected bursts up to 120 RPS for demo scenarios; average request ~350 tokens, 95th ~1200 tokens. See attached pp-traffic-matrix.csv.
4) PromptPilot performs light template-based rewrites; we attempt to preserve tokenization but there are occasional template expansions — we can provide sample templates.
5) Tracing: request/response ids, timing, token tallies are sufficient for initial rollout. We do not want raw prompts persisted in Redwood logs for privacy.

Our ideal MAP items:
- Week 0: NDA & SOW signed
- Week 1: adapter prototype + staging integration (LangChain -> PP -> Redwood)
- Week 2: streaming flow + basic tracing surface in Console
- Week 3: performance tuning and joint demo

We can share an NDA and SOW template this afternoon. Let us know your availability for Fri 10am PST or Mon 9am PST.

Attachments: pp-traffic-matrix.csv

Best,
Emma Lee
VP, Partnerships
PromptPilot

Thanks Emma — that's very helpful. Proposed next steps and timeline below (we'll call this an initial MAP). Please review and flag changes: 

Proposed 6-week pilot MAP (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): NDA executed, SOW template agreed, HubSpot deal created (PP-4732)
- Week 1: Adapter prototype (LangChain shim) + staging keys; basic end-to-end smoke test (no streaming)
- Week 2: Enable streaming; implement trace id propagation and token accounting events visible in Redwood Console
- Week 3: Performance baseline (p90/p95), initial tuning (batching/kv cache)
- Week 4: Joint customer-like demo, collect metrics and SLOs, iterate on prompt templates to reduce token inflation
- Week 5: Stabilization, run observability checks and regression tests; draft commercial terms based on measured unit economics
- Week 6: Wrap, handoff to Growth/Partnerships for GTM and recommended integration docs

Owners: PromptPilot provides templates and traffic samples (Emma). Redwood provides staging tenant, adapter template, and a runtime owner (Jonas). Vanessa will coordinate commercial touchpoints.

Open items for the sync:
- Which team signs SOW (legal lead)?
- Do you require a dedicated Dedicated (reserved) capacity trial vs hosted for the PoC?
- Acceptance criteria for streaming (max acceptable token loss, latency threshold).

We're available Mon 9am PST — I'll send calendar invite. I've also created a HubSpot deal link and added the MAP as a shared sheet.

Related links: https://hubspot.example/deal/PP-4732, https://app.docusign.com/link/abc123-promptpilot-sow

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Mina Haddad
